pins.description: Quantum Nematode's `wormlight.connectome/1` export: neurons, chemical synapses, gap junctions and neuromuscular connections
Fenyves et al. 2020, S1 Data (`journal.pcbi.1007974.s003`), sheet "5. Sign prediction"
Fenyves et al. 2020, S5 Data (`journal.pcbi.1007974.s007`), sheet "5. Sign prediction (Cook)"
Creamer, Leifer & Pillow's fitted weights, `quick_start_examples/model_weights.csv` in `Nondairy-Creamer/Creamer_LDS_2026`
The eigenworm basis of Stephens et al. 2008, as the Stephens group distributes it with WormPose: `extras/EigenWorms.csv`, 100 modes over 100 tangent angles

datasets.dataset: Cook et al. 2019, _Nature_ 571:63, in the corrected release of Emmons 2024, _PLoS Biol_ 22:e3002939, S1 File (`journal.pbio.3002939.s001`, "Connectome Adjacency Matrices")
datasets.takes: Hermaphrodite chemical synapses, gap junctions and neuromuscular connections, as EM serial-section counts
datasets.route: Quantum Nematode export, which vendors this file beside the 2019 original that nematode's own experiments keep using
datasets.licence: CC BY 4.0. Cite Cook et al. 2019 and Emmons 2024. The chemical matrix is identical to the 2019 original, including all 956 neuromuscular entries; the gap junctions carry the lab's July 2020 corrections and its 2023 BDU–ALM and BDU–PLM junctions. The 2019 supplement itself states no licence, which is why this release is used

notice.title: Connectome
notice.attribution: Cook SJ, Jarrell TA, Brittin CA, et al. Whole-animal connectomes of both Caenorhabditis elegans sexes. Nature 571:63–71 (2019), doi:10.1038/s41586-019-1352-7. As released in Emmons SW. Comprehensive analysis of the C. elegans connectome reveals novel circuits and functions of previously unstudied neurons. PLoS Biology 22(12):e3002939 (2024), doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.3002939, S1 File (doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.3002939.s001). Wormlight uses the hermaphrodite matrices' counts unchanged, restricted to the 302 neurons and the 95 body wall muscles, with the two directions of each gap junction folded into one pair and the 14 gap junctions between a neuron and itself omitted.

datasets.licence: CC BY 4.0 (eLife). Cite Wang et al. 2024

notice.title: Neurotransmitter identities
notice.attribution: Wang C, Vidal B, Sural S, et al. A neurotransmitter atlas of C. elegans males and hermaphrodites. eLife 13:RP95402 (2024), doi:10.7554/eLife.95402, Supplementary File 2. Quantum Nematode reads each neuron's release identities from it, excluding orphan and unknown entries, uptake-only entries, the atlas's hedged entries and one precursor.

datasets.dataset: OpenWorm ConnectomeToolbox (`cect`) `Cells.py`, v0.3.1, as curated into Quantum Nematode's neuron table
datasets.takes: Each neuron's class: sensory, interneuron, motor or pharyngeal
datasets.licence: MIT, Copyright (c) 2024 OpenWorm. cect attributes its classification to Cook et al. 2019 and WormAtlas

notice.title: Neuron classes
notice.attribution: Neuron classes from OpenWorm ConnectomeToolbox (cect) Cells.py v0.3.1, as curated in Quantum Nematode (https://github.com/SyntheticBrains/nematode, Apache-2.0).

datasets.takes: Soma positions, dendrite tips (where head sensory neurons sense) and process extents (touch receptive fields)
datasets.licence: MIT (c302). The morphologies come from the WormBase Virtual Worm (Grove & Sternberg), released into the public domain

notice.title: Neuron positions
notice.licence: MIT; licence text below. The underlying WormBase Virtual Worm model is in the public domain
notice.attribution: Neuron positions and process extents derived from the c302 NeuroML2 cell morphologies (OpenWorm, https://github.com/openworm/c302), which OpenWorm converted from the WormBase Virtual Worm, a 3D model of the worm made by Christian Grove and Paul Sternberg (Caltech).

datasets.dataset: Fenyves et al. 2020, _PLoS Comput Biol_ 16:e1007974, files `journal.pcbi.1007974.s003` (S1 Data, the WormWiring reconstruction) and `s007` (S5 Data, its "5. Sign prediction (Cook)" sheet)
datasets.takes: Synapse signs predicted from transmitter and receptor expression ("NT+R"), used where the presynaptic transmitter the prediction rests on is one of the cell's identities in Wang et al. 2024. The two files agree on all 3,121 connections they share
datasets.licence: CC BY 4.0. Cite Fenyves et al. 2020

notice.title: Synapse signs
notice.attribution: Fenyves BG, Szilágyi GS, Vassy Z, Sőti C, Csermely P. Synaptic polarity and sign-balance prediction using gene expression data in the Caenorhabditis elegans chemical synapse neuronal connectome network. PLoS Computational Biology 16(12):e1007974 (2020), doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1007974, S1 Data (doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1007974.s003) and S5 Data (doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1007974.s007). Wormlight takes the predicted polarity of each connection, and sets it aside where the presynaptic transmitter it rests on is not among the cell's identities in Wang et al. 2024.

datasets.takes: The port check runs Neural Interactome's own code on its Varshney et al. 2011 matrices, which are indexed [post, pre]

datasets.dataset: Creamer, Leifer & Pillow fitted weights (`Creamer_LDS_2026`, pinned from the authors' repository; nematode vendors the same file)
datasets.takes: The sign cross-check report on the 1,049 head connections they cover; never used as strengths
datasets.licence: MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Matthew S. Creamer. The cross-check report reproduces the licence text beside the weights it quotes

datasets.dataset: The eigenworms of Stephens et al. 2008, _PLoS Comput Biol_ 4:e1000028, as distributed by the authors' group with WormPose (Hebert et al. 2021; `iteal/wormpose`, `extras/EigenWorms.csv`, unchanged since its first commit in July 2020)
datasets.takes: Checkpoint 1's posture clause: the first four modes, with the head at angle 1. The file names no source; its identity with the 2008 basis is inferred: WormPose projects onto eigenworms citing Stephens et al. 2008, and the group's Broekmans et al. 2016 took its eigenworms from that paper; and and the 6,655 real postures in the OIST Physics of Behavior tutorials (Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.15099731, CC BY 4.0), which the tutorial introduces as coming from Stephens et al.'s experiment, are consistent with it: the first four modes capture 96.46% of their variance, against 96.48% for the best any four modes can do. That is an in-sample check, not independent confirmation
datasets.route: Downloaded and checked by the data build; read by the harness
datasets.licence: BSD-3-Clause, Copyright (c) 2020, Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology. Not redistributed: the build and the harness read it from its pinned URL

datasets.takes: Cited only. The OSF deposit states no licence, and the `wormneuroatlas` copy is GPL-3.0, so it can't be bundled with Apache-2.0 code

datasets.dataset: Levy & Bargmann 2020, `LevySagi/Adaptive-Concentration-Threshold` (CC BY 4.0 per its LICENSE)
datasets.takes: The adaptive-threshold constants K = 5.5 µM and τ = 17 s were read from `NoiseFilteringAnalysis_Fig6.m`. No code or data is bundled
Reviewed as prior art. Its muscle map is not used, because Wormlight takes neuromuscular connections straight from Cook et al. 2019

datasets.dataset: Boyle, Berri & Cohen 2012, the model's source code (`worm.cc`)
datasets.takes: Consulted for how the whole-worm drag is split per rod. No code is bundled

datasets.dataset: Ji et al. 2021 data and code (Dryad, doi:10.5061/dryad.wwpzgmsk2)
datasets.takes: Not used directly; the head switch's parameters are taken from the paper

datasets.dataset: Cook et al. 2019 SI 5, original and "corrected July 2020" versions (wormwiring.org; the original is vendored in nematode via cect)
datasets.takes: Compared cell by cell with Emmons 2024's S1 File: identical chemical synapses, and gap junctions that differ only by the 2020 corrections and the 2023 BDU junctions. Neither states a licence; WormWiring shows only "Emmons Lab Copyright (c) 2020"
